result.description: WHITELINE TRANSPORT (AUST.) PTY. LTD.  The Diesel Motor Mechanic will be responsible for inspecting, diagnosing, servicing, repairing, and maintaining heavy diesel-powered vehicles, trailers, and associated mechanical systems to ensure maximum fleet reliability, safety, and operational efficiency. The successful candidate will carry out preventative maintenance, fault diagnosis, and repairs while ensuring all work complies with manufacturer specifications, Australian Standards, and workplace health and safety requirements.  This role is ideal for a motivated tradesperson with strong diagnostic skills and experience working on heavy commercial vehicles.   Benefits   Competitive salary package  Full-time permanent employment  Stable long-term career opportunity  Modern workshop with quality diagnostic equipment  Work on a well-maintained fleet of heavy vehicles  Ongoing technical training and professional development  Supportive and safety-focused team environment  Career progression opportunities within a growing transport business  Employee recognition and long-term employment prospects    Task & responsibilities   Inspect, diagnose, service, repair, and maintain diesel engines, transmissions, braking systems, steering, suspension, and driveline components.  Perform scheduled preventative maintenance on heavy vehicles and trailers.  Diagnose mechanical, hydraulic, pneumatic, electrical, and electronic faults using specialised diagnostic equipment.  Repair or replace defective components, parts, and assemblies.  Conduct engine tuning and performance testing to ensure optimal vehicle operation.  Perform servicing in accordance with manufacturer specifications and maintenance schedules.  Inspect vehicles to ensure compliance with roadworthiness, safety, and regulatory requirements.  Complete work orders, maintenance reports, service records, and parts documentation accurately.  Maintain workshop equipment, tools, and work areas in a safe and clean condition.  Assist with breakdown repairs and emergency maintenance when required.  Liaise with workshop supervisors regarding repair priorities and maintenance scheduling.  Ensure compliance with workplace health and safety (WHS) policies and environmental procedures.  Identify opportunities to improve maintenance efficiency and minimise vehicle downtime.  Support apprentices and junior mechanics where required.    Qualification & experience   AQF Certificate III in Heavy Commercial Vehicle Mechanical Technology, Automotive Diesel Engine Technology, or an equivalent recognised trade qualification.   Minimum three year of relevant full-time experience  as a Diesel Motor Mechanic working on heavy commercial vehicles.  Demonstrated experience servicing and repairing diesel engines, heavy trucks, trailers, and associated mechanical systems.  Strong diagnostic and fault-finding skills using modern diagnostic equipment.  Sound knowledge of diesel fuel systems, braking systems, transmissions, hydraulics, and electrical systems.  Ability to interpret workshop manuals, technical drawings, and service documentation.  Strong commitment to workplace health and safety and quality workmanship.  Good communication, organisational, and problem-solving skills.   About Company     WHITELINE TRANSPORT (AUST.) PTY. LTD.  is a leading Australian transport and logistics company providing reliable metropolitan, regional, and interstate freight solutions. Operating a modern fleet of heavy vehicles and trailers, the company is committed to delivering safe, efficient, and dependable transport services across Australia. With a strong focus on operational excellence, fleet reliability, workplace safety, and customer satisfaction, WHITELINE TRANSPORT (AUST.) PTY. LTD. continually invests in its people, equipment, and maintenance programs to support the highest industry standards. result.description: Cox Purtell Most organisations either have an AI strategist who can't build, or a builder who has no seat at the table. This role offers a rare chance to stay close to the tech, while also having a seat at the table.  A large higher education organisation is bringing in a Head of AI Delivery to own applied AI end to end: shape where it goes, and build the systems that get it there. This is not a hands-off strategy seat, and it is not a pure build seat. It is both, deliberately.   What you'll own:  - Direct input into the organisation's AI roadmap and strategic digital plan - not just executing someone else's - End-to-end delivery of agentic AI, generative AI, LLM and RAG-based systems from concept to production - Establishing the AI capability function from scratch - tooling, delivery patterns, operating model - Mentoring and uplifting existing staff as you build the function around you - Governance, risk, and responsible AI as a core pillar, not an afterthought - transparency, bias mitigation, post-deployment monitoring - Enterprise architecture and cloud platform decisions (Azure, AWS, GCP) - Direct engagement with the CIO, COO, and senior executive leadership   Who you'll report to:  The CIO - technically astute, commercially savvy, and driven to produce outcomes. You'll also be visible to the COO and senior executive leadership. What you build gets seen, and it's expected to demonstrate real value within the first 3-6 months.   What you need:  - You've shipped AI or ML into production before, in a real enterprise - not just a lab or a pilot - You've built or led an AI capability function from the ground up - You've worked hands-on with agentic AI and multi-agent orchestration, not just read about it - RAG, prompt engineering, MLOps/LLMOps - you've actually done this work, not sat in on it - You take governance and responsible AI seriously, in a regulated or genuinely complex environment - You're comfortable being watched by executives and the board, not just your manager   The setup:  - Brisbane-based, hybrid - 2-3 days on-site - Contracted as 12-month fixed-term, but the engagement runs multi-year - real security, not a cliff-edge contract - $180,000-$220,000 plus superannuation - Relocation support available - Standard benefits including leave loading and salary packaging  One non-negotiable: you'll need Australian citizenship or permanent residency for this one.  You'll thrive here if you want both the seat at the table and your hands on the keyboard. You'll struggle here if you only want one or the other - this role won't let you pick.  Want the full brief?
